clue.text: Approval of taste shown? Left off…

indicators.note: something taken off is removed, so the word for left comes out

parts.note: a taste is a flavour

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether liking a dish shows good taste, then trails off mid-sentence.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs this clue on into 4 across for the surface only; 'off' removes L from FLAVOUR.
explanation.definitionFit: To find favour with someone is to win their approval, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: A possibly acceptable form of. pleonasm

definitions.text: A possibly acceptable form of. pleonasm

parts.words: A possibly acceptable form of. pleonasm
parts.note: a pleonasm uses redundant words; this phrase is the marketing example where a gift is by nature already without charge

explanation.surface: A remark about a form of redundant wording that might be tolerated.
explanation.walkthrough: The full stop after 'of' is a printing flaw.
explanation.definitionFit: Every present costs nothing to its receiver, so the advertiser's two-word phrase repeats itself, a textbook redundancy.

clue.text: Turn up in revue, not con-. cerned with fashion

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so one piece sits within the other
not means take away, so the letters for concerning come out

parts.note: taken as written
RE means concerning or about

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means read from the bottom, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: a go is a turn

explanation.surface: A performer turns up in a revue, not bothered about fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: The line break split 'concerned' in print. 'not' takes the word for concerning out of the show, leaving VUE; 'up' turns the word for a turn backwards, and 'in' sets that inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Vogue means the prevailing fashion or style.

clue.text: German town provided some wonderful memories

indicators.note: some means only part of the following words, so the letters lie within them

explanation.surface: Someone recalls happy times in a German town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' points to letters spanning 'wonderfUL Memories'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ulm is a city on the Danube in southern Germany.

clue.text: …to supply notes about brew that's wonderful

indicators.note: about means placed around, so one word wraps the other here

parts.note: singing supplies musical notes, so this phrase means sing
mash is the brewing mixture of malt and hot water

explanation.surface: Carrying on from 1 across: someone offers to sing about a wonderful home brew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to supply notes' is a verb phrase for making music with the voice; 'about' wraps it around the brewing word.
explanation.definitionFit: Smashing is informal British praise meaning excellent or terrific.

clue.text: Such a state of bliss may be spoilt if one intrudes

indicators.note: something that intrudes pushes in, so this letter goes inside the word

parts.note: marred means spoilt
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Wedded bliss may be ruined if a third party interferes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'intrudes' puts I inside MARRED.
explanation.definitionFit: Wedlock is traditionally described as a state of happiness, so being wed is such a state.

clue.text: Vehicle designed for particularly long journeys

definitions.text: Vehicle designed for particularly long journeys

parts.words: Vehicle designed for particularly long journeys
parts.note: suggests a car built for long distances, but it is the car itself that is extra long

explanation.surface: A description of a car built for long trips.
explanation.walkthrough: 'long' describes the vehicle's length, not the length of the trip.
explanation.definitionFit: This luxury car has an extended body, giving rides that are long in a quite different sense.

clue.text: Page in one volume is edited, leaving nothing rash

indicators.note: edited means revised and reworked, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
taken as written
taken as written
O is the round figure zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A page in a single volume is revised, and nothing rash is left in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'edited' rearranges P, I, VOLUME and IS, and 'leaving' says O (nothing) is left out of the result.
explanation.definitionFit: Impulsive means acting without thinking, which is a synonym of rash.

clue.text: Community energy, and bit of work, raised the country

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means turned upwards, so the joined pieces read backwards

parts.note: EC is the European Community
E is the symbol for energy
an erg is a small unit of work in physics

explanation.surface: A European community gathers energy and work to lift up its country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' reverses EC + E + ERG to read GREECE.
explanation.definitionFit: Greece is a nation in south-east Europe, a member of the European Community.

clue.text: Basic security device

definitions.meaning: a basic item is a standard or chief one, as in a basic food
a bent wire fastener that holds papers or a hasp secure

explanation.definitionFit: A staple is both a main commodity and a U-shaped metal fastening.

clue.text: Greet more structured measure of exercise

indicators.note: structured means built into a new arrangement, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An instruction to greet more people in a structured exercise class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'structured' tells you to rearrange GREET MORE.
explanation.definitionFit: An ergometer is a device such as an exercise bike that measures the work done by the user.

clue.text: Established change in India

annotationWithheld.why: Established change in India (5): 'change in India' defines RUPEE, but no parse of 'Established' gives any letters of it; the scan prints the same words and a search found no explanation

clue.text: The make-up of a company, at various stages

definitions.text: The make-up of a company, at various stages

parts.words: The make-up of a company, at various stages
parts.note: reads as how a business is made up as it grows, but means the cosmetics a theatre company wears on stage

explanation.surface: A description of how a firm is made up as it develops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'company' is a troupe of actors and 'stages' are theatre stages, not phases.
explanation.definitionFit: Actors wear this oily cosmetic as stage make-up in theatre productions.

clue.text: Type of bird, dog or butterfly

parts.note: the swallow is a kind of bird
to dog someone is to tail them

explanation.surface: A list of things this word might name: a bird, a dog or a butterfly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dog' is a verb meaning follow, not an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The swallowtail is a large butterfly with tail-like streamers on its hind wings.

clue.text: Finally abandoned need for resin

indicators.note: the end of the word is abandoned, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: a need is a lack

explanation.surface: Someone at last gives up needing resin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finally abandoned' removes the last letter of LACK.
explanation.definitionFit: Lac is the resin secreted by insects and used to make shellac.

clue.text: Film showing old dog intercepting the enemy

indicators.note: something intercepting gets in the way, so these letters sit inside the other word

parts.note: a foe is an enemy
to dog someone is to tag along after them

explanation.surface: A movie in which an elderly dog cuts off the enemy's advance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dog' is a verb meaning follow; 'intercepting' sets the old dog inside the enemy, after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Footage is recorded film, a length of filmed material.

clue.text: Patent nearly secured surprisingly quickly?

indicators.note: secured means held fast inside, so one word encloses the other

parts.note: patent means obvious, overt
nigh means nearly

explanation.surface: A patent was obtained almost suspiciously fast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Patent' means obvious here, not a licence; 'secured' sets the word for nearly inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An overnight success happens suddenly, with a speed that surprises.

clue.text: Feel bad, conned about plant

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the joined words are read backwards

parts.note: to ail is to feel unwell
to be had is to be conned

explanation.surface: Someone feels bad after being tricked over a plant they bought.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns the two joined words round together, so the plant's name reads from their last letter back.
explanation.definitionFit: The dahlia is a garden flower with large showy blooms, so it is a kind of plant.

clue.text: Almost understood content of composer, except a basic element

indicators.note: content of means held within, so one piece goes inside the other
except means leaving out, so the letter a is removed

parts.note: Haydn was an Austrian composer

indicators.note: almost means nearly whole, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: Roger is radio language for message understood

explanation.surface: Someone almost grasps what a composer's work contains, apart from one basic element.
explanation.walkthrough: 'except a' drops that letter from the composer's name, giving HYDN; 'Almost' trims the radio word for understood, and 'content of' sets the trimmed word inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Hydrogen is the simplest chemical element, number one in the periodic table.

clue.text: Briefly have to consider rejected manuscript

parts.note: have shortened is the contraction 've

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so this word is read backwards

parts.note: to mull over is to consider

explanation.surface: An editor quickly reads and turns down a manuscript.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Briefly have' is the contraction, as in I've; 'rejected' sends the word for consider backwards, giving LLUM.
explanation.definitionFit: Vellum is fine parchment, and by extension a manuscript written on it.

clue.text: Engaged in getting into young female English artist

indicators.note: getting into means entering, so these letters go inside the word

parts.note: a miss is a girl or young woman
to be at something is to be engaged in it

explanation.surface: A young Englishwoman who is engaged to be married takes up art.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Engaged' hints at a betrothal but means busy at something; 'getting into' sets that word inside the girl's title, just after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Henri Matisse was a French painter, a leading artist of the twentieth century.

clue.text: Rather nervous and timid, touring Bucks town

indicators.note: touring means going round, so one word surrounds the other

parts.note: shy means timid
Iver is a village-town in Buckinghamshire, abbreviated Bucks

explanation.surface: A nervous, timid person on a tour of a Buckinghamshire town.
explanation.walkthrough: Bucks is short for Buckinghamshire, an English county, and the town is a small place there; 'touring' wraps the timid word around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Shivery means trembling or a little jittery, as a nervous person might feel.

clue.text: Second time took a lift — or walked?

parts.note: to take a lift is to ride, so rode

explanation.surface: Someone asks if they were given a ride a second time or went on foot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'took a lift' means accepted a ride, not used an elevator.
explanation.definitionFit: Strode means walked with long steps.

clue.text: The same two children looking up an antelope

indicators.note: in a down clue looking up means read upwards, so the letters run backwards
the same word twice over, so this piece is repeated

parts.note: a kid is a child

explanation.surface: Two identical children gaze up at an antelope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The same two' doubles KID; 'looking up' reverses the pair.
explanation.definitionFit: The dik-dik is a tiny African antelope.

clue.text: What's. charged by one working?

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: Asking what gets charged by someone at work.
explanation.walkthrough: The stray full stop after 'What's' is a printing flaw.
explanation.definitionFit: An ion is an atom or molecule carrying an electric charge.

clue.text: Artistic production not using interpretation of 12?

definitions.text: Artistic production not using interpretation of 12?

parts.words: Artistic production not using interpretation of 12?
parts.note: reads 12 across as two words, oily paint, so the artwork wanted is one made without oils

explanation.surface: An artwork that does not follow a theatrical interpretation.
explanation.walkthrough: 12 across split as GREASE PAINT suggests oil paint; this work uses another medium.
explanation.definitionFit: A painting made with pigments thinned in water, rather than oil-based paints.

clue.text: Repeated round-the-world trip

parts.note: sounds like a traveller's world tour but means the path a satellite circles again and again

explanation.surface: A traveller makes the global tour more than once.
explanation.definitionFit: A satellite's circuit around the Earth is one such path, travelled over and over.

clue.text: In the morning — what a surprise! —- back to hidebound opinion

indicators.note: back means read in reverse, so the joined pieces run backwards

parts.note: AM stands for ante meridiem, in the morning
God! is an exclamation of surprise

explanation.surface: Someone startled in the morning returns to their narrow views.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns the time of day and the exclamation round together, so the opinion reads from their last letter back.
explanation.definitionFit: Dogma is a set of beliefs held rigidly and without question.

clue.text: Lad with badges fixed here, on, the back of his bike?

definitions.text: here, on, the back of his bike

indicators.note: fixed means put right or reassembled, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A boy has badges attached to the rear of his bicycle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fixed' looks like attached but signals the rearrangement; the commas around 'on' are a print quirk.
explanation.definitionFit: A saddlebag is a pouch that hangs behind the seat of a bicycle.

clue.text: Brass rim

definitions.meaning: brass means cheek or impudence, as in brass neck
the edge of a cup or wound

explanation.definitionFit: Lip is both slang for insolent talk and the edge of a vessel.

clue.text: Woman eager to entertain half of the Olympic team?

indicators.note: to entertain is to hold or host, so one word takes the other inside

parts.note: keen means eager

indicators.note: half the word is kept, so the second four letters are dropped

parts.note: an Olympic team is made up of athletes

explanation.surface: A keen woman hosting half the national Olympic squad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half of' keeps the first four letters of the sporting word, ATHL; 'to entertain' puts them inside the eager word.
explanation.definitionFit: Kathleen is a woman's first name.

clue.text: Precise type of club, where tee's involved

indicators.note: involved means drawn in, so this letter goes inside the word

parts.note: a spoon is an old name for a lofted wooden golf club
tee is the spelt name of the letter T

explanation.surface: A golfer picks the exact club wherever the tee is set.
explanation.walkthrough: A SPOON is an old golf club; 'involved' puts T inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Spot on is British informal for exactly right or accurate.
